newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed in uneventful trade.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed in uneventful trade.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mixed, with yen contracts edging off highs in uneventful trade, but awash in speculation on the U.S.'s dollar policy, traders and analysts said.

The confusion stemming from a key Japanese official's bearish dollar/yen comments earlier in the week is expected to keep December yen rangebound between $0.009135 and $0.008816, or 110.00 and 114.00 spot in the intermediate term, they said.
"Unless there is some new surprise, we would be surprised to see levels violated on the (dollar's) downside," David Schoenthal, senior managing director at Bear Stearns, said.

Most traders agreed, adding that December yen was likely to tread near $0.00880, rather than $0.009100. Some traders believe December will have difficulty rising to $0.009061, or 110.90 spot, which is the dollar's one-month low.
One French-based firm sold about 1,000 December yen at the $0.008992 level, while a Japanese firm was one of the last firms to attempt selling 1,500 in the all-or-nothing pit.

"Someone is trying to trade something in the cash market, because that 1,500 offer keeps popping up in the pit," one floor trader said, adding that the offer came into the pit from several different firms in the last 20 minutes of trade.
One technical analyst said December yen would have to close above $0.009100, or about 109.90 spot, to signal a reversal.
"We really have no change in direction," he said. "There is no inkling the downtrend from May 1995 is over."
He said December marks were attempting to reverse their downtrend, as the contract pressed near the 1-1/2-month high of $0.6680, or about 1.50 spot, in light afternoon trade.
"December is really hemmed in here between $0.6500 (1.54 spot) and $0.6701 (1.4940 spot)," he said. Resistance is at $0.6900 (1.45 spot) and $0.6925 (1.4454 spot), he said.
He said support was at $1.6370 and $1.6250, with resistance at the contract high of $1.6484, which was set on Friday, and at $1.6575.
December Canadian dollars are seen rising to $0.7460 in the near term.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was up $0.000026 at $0.008984, marks were up $0.0038 at $0.6663, Swiss francs were $0.0053 higher at $0.7930, sterling was flat at $1.6466, Canadian dollars were down $0.0004 at $0.7532, Australian dollars were $0.0038 higher at $0.7866 and Mexican pesos were $0.000700 at $0.123575.
Schoenthal said profit-taking is likely to occur in the dollar/mark and dollar/Swiss franc next week. On cash crosses, marks slipped against yen on an unwinding of long positions.
"Swiss francs are in a confirmed downtrend," the technician said. December Swiss francs is likely to test the contract low of $0.7811 set during Wednesday's GLOBEX session.
Further support is seen at $0.7780, or 1.2900 spot.
While sterling futures closed unchanged, and Canadian dollars ended slightly lower, both currencies are in strong uptrends, traders and analysts said.
"Support is so far below, it's ridiculous," a trader said.
